content.text:
karpathy/autoresearch is a Python repo for AI agents that automatically run research loops around single-GPU nanochat training.

The surprising part is the scope: not “use an LLM to answer research questions,” but use agents to operate the experiment loop itself. The repo context frames it as AI agents doing frontier-style research work that humans used to coordinate through meetings, notes, and manual iteration.

Why developers are paying attention: it points at a very concrete version of “AI for AI research.” The target is small enough to reason about — nanochat training on a single GPU — instead of an abstract cluster-scale agent swarm. That makes the idea easier to inspect, reproduce, or adapt if you already work with training scripts, eval loops, or experiment automation.

At a plain technical level, the interesting bit is the wrapper around training. The core workload is still model training. The “autoresearch” layer is about automating what happens around it: deciding what to try next, running the training job, observing outputs, and continuing the loop. Python is a natural fit here because it can glue together scripts, configs, logs, model runs, and agent calls.

Caveat: there are no star or growth signals provided here, and the description is based on the repo context rather than independently verified results. So this is worth treating as an early/interesting research-engineering artifact, not proof that autonomous AI research is solved.

If you were building this kind of loop, what would you let the agent control first: hyperparameters, architecture changes, data, or eval design?
